findings.evidence: Container: toast, Fires: on-focus. Message reports a blocking condition (reset link expired) that cannot be worked around on the current screen.
findings.fix: Show this message in a modal dialog that does not auto-clear, so the reader cannot miss the explanation for the blocking failure. The dialog should also include the offered action (send a new link button) prominently.
findings.violation: Password reset link expiration is a fully blocking failure that prevents the reader from proceeding with password reset. A self-clearing toast is inappropriate for a blocking failure; the reader may miss the one message explaining why reset cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Acknowledge the gravity of the situation and the reader's frustration. Add a sincere tone: 'Unfortunately, your changes couldn't be saved and we weren't able to recover them. Please contact our support team - they can review what happened and help get your work back if possible.'
findings.violation: Unrecoverable failure (lost changes cannot be recovered) is presented as a bare technical notice with minimal acknowledgment of what this means for the reader and what they have lost.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Predictable mistake: yes, Fires: on-submit. File format validation can be performed when the user selects the file, not deferred until form submission.
findings.fix: Validate file format client-side as soon as the user selects a file. Show a real-time warning if an unsupported format is selected, letting the reader correct it immediately rather than after filling out the rest of the form.
findings.violation: File-format error (PDF/PNG only) is a predictable and foreseeable mistake the system could catch during file selection, but the validation fires only on-submit instead of warning during entry.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page.
findings.fix: Place the message directly below the password field so the reader encounters the requirement just before or as they enter the field, not earlier in the form.
findings.violation: Password requirement message appears at the top of a long form, but the password field is below, requiring the reader to scroll to see both the message and the field together.

findings.evidence: Container: inline. Message reports a completed, unrecoverable loss (changes not saved and cannot be recovered).
findings.fix: Show this message in a modal dialog so the reader cannot miss it and understands the severity. The visual weight and blocking nature of a modal matches the gravity of the situation (lost work).
findings.violation: Total, unrecoverable failure (changes lost) is shown as an inline message. A critical failure that blocks recovery should use a modal container to ensure the reader sees and understands the severity.
